title: OTTO-CHARGE ARM
frame: Arm base frame: origin on J1 axis at the mount collar top, +Y up, +Z toward the car, X along the car. Zero pose (all joints 0).

subsystems.name: Riser and mount
subsystems.function: A steel riser on the charger pad carries the arm. Its J1 axis is 550 mm above the deck and 2.82 m from the car centreline.
how: 4 chemical anchors M16 hold the riser to the concrete pad.
8 screws M12 hold the mount plate to the riser.
The cable trunk joins the riser to the charger cabinet. The power and data cables run inside it.

subsystems.name: J1 base yaw
subsystems.function: Turns the whole arm about the vertical axis to face the charge port.
how: A size 40 actuator in the riser top turns the turret.
Range is +/- 180 degrees. Cables pass through the hollow shaft.

subsystems.name: J2 shoulder pitch
subsystems.function: Leans the upper arm toward or away from the car. It carries the highest load of any joint.
how: A size 50 actuator in the turret boss drives the upper arm.
A nitrogen gas spring balancer carries most of the gravity load, so the gear and brake see less.

subsystems.name: Upper arm
subsystems.function: The 1.344 m cast link from the shoulder to the elbow.
how: A hollow aluminium casting, 7 mm wall.
Its cheek bolts to the J2 output. Its boss clamps the J3 actuator.

subsystems.name: J3 elbow pitch
subsystems.function: Folds the forearm to set the reach and the height of the wrist.
how: A size 40 actuator in the upper arm boss drives the forearm.

subsystems.name: Forearm
subsystems.function: The 1.142 m cast link from the elbow to the wrist centre.
how: A hollow aluminium casting. Its top socket holds the J4 actuator.

subsystems.name: Spherical wrist (J4, J5, J6)
subsystems.function: Points the connector along the port axis. The 3 wrist axes meet at one point, so position and angle solve apart.
how: J4 rolls the forearm end (size 25).
J5 pitches the wrist (size 25).
J6 rolls the tool (size 20). Its output is the tool flange (ISO 9409-1).

subsystems.name: Connector tool
subsystems.function: Finds the inlet, plugs in, latches, and lets go. It measures the force on every move.
how: A 6-axis force and torque sensor reads the insertion force.
A compliance unit lets the connector float up to 6 mm and 3 degrees, so a small error cannot jam it.
Stereo cameras and a time-of-flight sensor find the inlet. A light ring helps at night.
A solenoid latch locks the connector in the inlet for the charge.

subsystems.name: Cable dress pack
subsystems.function: Carries the charge cable and the signal lines along the arm without strain.
how: Clamps on each link hold the liquid-cooled cable.
A loop at each joint lets it turn.

subsystems.name: Safety and status
subsystems.function: Stops the arm when a person comes near and shows its state to the site.
how: A safety laser scanner on the riser watches the stall at knee height.
An emergency stop on the riser cuts motor power (safe torque off).
Light rings on J2 and the wrist show the state: teal ready, amber moving, green charging, red fault.
